sections.content: You know *hubiera* and *hubiese* + past participle from B2 Unit 16 in past unreal conditions (*Si hubiéramos salido antes*) and past clauses of doubt (*No creía que hubieran terminado*), paired with *habría llegado* from B2 Unit 10. In historiography and essays on memory, the pluperfect subjunctive serves two central tasks: weighing counterfactual turns of history (*si se hubiera catalogado*) and expressing past-tense regret, surprise or scepticism about even earlier events (*lamentaban que no se hubiesen recogido los testimonios*). Both *-ra* and *-se* forms are fully accepted in every subjunctive clause here.

sections.title: Counterfactual and retrospective frames
rows: Si se hubiera catalogado el inventario, el manuscrito no se habría perdido.
Past counterfactual condition (*si* + pluperfect subjunctive) + conditional perfect result.
Lamentaban que no se hubiesen recogido aquellos testimonios a tiempo.
Past emotion about an earlier omission (*lamentaban que* + pluperfect subjunctive).
Nadie imaginaba entonces que aquella inscripción hubiera trascendido tantas décadas.
Past disbelief about an earlier achievement.
Dudaban de que el barrio hubiera conservado su trazado sin la oposición vecinal.
Past doubt about a prior outcome.

items.spanish: Si el municipio hubiera promovido la conmemoración antes, más testigos habrían participado.
items.english: If the municipality had promoted the commemoration earlier, more witnesses would have taken part.

items.spanish: Los cronistas lamentaron que se hubiesen perdido las cartas que la familia había prometido legar.
items.english: The chroniclers regretted that the letters the family had promised to bequeath had been lost.

items.spanish: Nadie en la comisión creía que un anacronismo tan evidente hubiera pasado inadvertido.
items.english: Nobody on the committee believed that such an obvious anachronism had gone unnoticed.

items.spanish: La historiografía actual señala que, sin aquellos diarios, casi nada habría llegado a la posteridad.
items.english: Contemporary historiography points out that, without those diaries, almost nothing would have reached posterity.

sections.content: Never put the conditional (*habría*) inside the *si* clause: write *si hubiera conservado*, never *si habría conservado*. Remember also that *hubiera* and *hubiese* are interchangeable here, and the participle stays invariable (*hubieran recogido*, never *hubieran recogidos*).
